messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — OpalPay is evaluating a drop-in swap from CompetitorY to Redwood. They want a 2-week POC to validate response parity, billing deltas, and networking before committing.
Priya: What are their non-negotiables?
Jordan: EU-only hosting for the POC, whitelisted egress IPs, compatibility with an existing proxy layer they run, and a short SOW with pilot pricing. Rough usage: ~4M tokens for the two weeks.
Priya: OK. Finance: can we do credits + discounted pilot rate?
Ken: We can offer €8k in credits + a 25% pilot discount if they sign a 3-month reserved minimum after the POC. Need legal to approve contractual language around token accounting differences.
Diego: Quick tech notes after looking at CompetitorY's responses: they return chat as messages[{role,content}] and streaming uses chunked JSON patches with seq ids. Redwood returns streaming SSE events with type:delta and our chat shape is outputs[] with metadata. Adapter needs to: preserve client message ids, map roles, and translate SSE->patch frames.
Diego: Example shim (concept):
```js
// shim: CompetitorY client expects incremental patches like {seq:123, delta:"..."}
redwoodSSE.on('data', (evt)=>{
  if (evt.type === 'delta') {
    sendToClient(JSON.stringify({seq: nextSeq++, delta: evt.data}));
  }
});
```
Hannah: Security flags: OpalPay requires audit logs for all requests (90 days), KMS-managed keys for at-rest, and completion of their questionnaire v2.0. They also asked about incident SLA and subprocessor list. I uploaded preliminary answers.
SecBot: Questionnaire uploaded: https://redwood.internal/sec/opalpay/q-3282 12/ SOC2 kit, encrypt-at-rest details, and subprocessor list attached.
Diego: A few behavioral deltas to call out to OpalPay in the SOW:
- Tokenization variance: our tokenizer yields ~6% fewer tokens on their corpora -> billing delta. We'll include a token-sample report.
- Stop behavior: Redwood occasionally includes trailing punctuation where CompetitorY truncates; we'll surface this in the eval.
- Embeddings: CompetitorY returns 1536 dim vectors; our chosen model returns 1024 dim vectors for the POC. We will provide a small conversion strategy (PCA fallback or reranker shim) — need product sign-off.
Priya: Good catch on embeddings. Product: can we support a compatibility embedding endpoint that pads/truncates to match dims for the POC?
Diego: We can provide a temporary compat endpoint that returns a 1536-length vector by appending zeros + a hash-derived sentinel; it's brittle but OK for demo. Will log a compatibility flag.
Ken: Legal: require statement in SOW about "no-quality-warranty" for adapter parity and explicit acceptance tests. I'll draft.
Priya: Ops: can we provide a static egress IP list for the POC and run in eu-west-1?
Diego: Yes — ops can allocate a small pool, but note that Dedicated/VPC is needed for permanent IPs; hosted POC will use ephemeral pool and we can publish the CIDR.
Hannah: Also they require IDS alerts forwarded to their SIEM via syslog. Ops: do we support that for POCs?
Diego: We can stream a subset of logs to a temporary syslog endpoint for the POC. Will validate PII filters first.
Priya: Action items:
- Diego: ship Node + Python shim, plus a smoke harness that runs their 50-core prompts and compares outputs (by Tue).
- Ken: draft SOW with pilot pricing + parity disclaimer (EOD Wed).
- Hannah: finish questionnaire responses and confirm syslog hookup (tomorrow).
- Ops (Emily): publish eu-west-1 CIDR list and runbook for whitelisting (today).
SecBot: Reminder will ping OpalPay in 36h if questionnaire not acknowledged.
Jordan: We'll ask OpalPay to sign a simple acceptance test matrix: 80% match on intent labels, vector cosine thresholds for embeddings, and streaming event ordering. If they accept, finance will trigger the pilot credits.
Priya: Scheduling: quick sync Mon 0900 CET to review the harness results. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
